 This is bounded local capture recovery, not completeness: process death before acknowledged capture, legacy/old-consumer retries, DLQ/quarantine, SDK logical-event collisions, late-hour fold repair, exceptional object fragmentation and deployed performance remain open. Fresh barrier checks are not an atomic global erasure fence; pre-cutoff races, ETag ABA, concurrent journal coordination and manifest omissions remain limitations. Claim lifecycle/retention and operational activation require their respective approvals; the flag is default-off and no deployment is implied.
 
-The consumer validates each complete ledger envelope before grouped persistence; an invalid row rejects its whole envelope without blocking valid siblings. Unversioned and `version:1` legacy messages without a delivery ID remain supported. Other explicit versions, malformed/empty sets, invalid explicit delivery IDs and caller-supplied reserved provenance are rejected, never partially filtered. Its ordered per-envelope `ack`/`retry` dispositions control queue acknowledgement; missing dispositions retry. `ok` is false if any envelope retries, and `skipped` counts rejected envelopes, not acknowledged drops or individual rows. Successful erasure suppression can acknowledge. Shared storage/barrier/capture failure retries the admitted cohort because aggregate partial counts do not prove individual completion. This does not add quarantine/DLQ or prevent retry exhaustion; legacy partial writes can still duplicate. A completely removed managed ID is indistinguishable from legitimate legacy input. Producer activation remains separate.
+The consumer validates each complete ledger envelope before grouped persistence; an invalid row rejects its whole envelope without blocking valid siblings. Unversioned and `version:1` legacy messages without a delivery ID remain supported. Other explicit versions, malformed/empty sets, invalid explicit delivery IDs and caller-supplied reserved provenance are rejected, never partially filtered. Its ordered per-envelope `ack`/`retry` dispositions control queue acknowledgement; missing or malformed positional proof retries. `ok` is false if any envelope retries, and `skipped` counts rejected envelopes, not acknowledged drops or individual rows. A managed delivery acknowledges only when every partition is definitely stored, already present or suppressed by erasure; partial or uncertain completion retries. Conflicting occurrences of one delivery ID all retry, while disjoint identities and destinations can proceed through the same grouped sink. Immutable claims are never rerouted, and a failed shared destination can retry all its deliveries. Initial tenant-barrier failure starts no writes. Managed and legacy persistence complete independently; legacy storage failure retries the entire legacy cohort, and its partial write counts remain a lower bound. This does not provide operational quarantine/replay or prevent all retry exhaustion; legacy partial writes can still duplicate. A completely removed managed ID is indistinguishable from legitimate legacy input. Producer activation remains separate.
 
 Ledger point lookup and replay reconcile every observed range candidate before returning a record or not-found. Exact full-payload decision and validated nonce-outcome retries coalesce; only valid top-level delivery metadata is excluded from comparison. Conflicting payloads, repeated nonce-free legacy outcomes, invalid product receipts, missing/malformed candidate inputs or broken pagination refuse with503 on enforced operator routes. Queries allow at most800 unique candidate objects,16MiB per object and in total, and1,000,000 listing/row/comparison work units; key/cursor strings are capped at2048 UTF-8 bytes and charged as listing work. Native bodies are read with bounded fatal-UTF-8 decoding; text-only adapters check actual bytes after materialization. These reads make no ledger writes and retain authorization, audit and erasure checks. They depend on truthful range names and the returned inventory, without snapshot isolation, detection of unlisted data, historical repair or end-to-end delivery/completeness assurance.
